title: Binary, hex and two's complement: how a chip stores minus five
examples: How do you write minus 5 in two's complement?
How do I convert binary to hex?
What is the range of an 8-bit signed number?

explain.say: In December 2014 the Gangnam Style video passed just over 2.1 billion views, the biggest number a signed 32-bit counter can hold, and YouTube had to switch to 64 bits. So how does a chip store numbers, even negative ones, with only ones and zeros? Look at the board: we will turn plus five into minus five.

draw.text: Binary, hex and two's complement: how a chip stores minus five

stages.note: Start with the positive number in 8 bits

stages.label: Flip: 1111 1010

explain.say: Start at the first box. Binary is base two: each bit is worth double the bit on its right, so 0000 0101 means four plus one, five. Hexadecimal, or hex, packs four bits into one symbol from 0 to F, which is why engineers love it. What is 1111 in decimal?

stages.note: Start with the positive number in 8 bits

stages.label: Flip: 1111 1010
stages.ask: Why do you flip the bits and add one?

stages.label: Hex: FB
stages.ask: How do I convert binary to hex?

explain.say: Now the trick. To make minus five, flip every bit, then add one. See the third box: 1111 1011. This is two's complement, and its beauty is that ordinary adding just works: five plus minus five gives 1 0000 0000, the ninth bit falls off, and zero is left. Can you see why the chip needs no separate subtract circuit?

stages.label: Flip: 1111 1010
stages.ask: Why do you flip the bits and add one?

explain.say: Look at the sorted patterns. In two's complement the leftmost bit, the most significant bit or MSB, shows the sign: 0 for positive, 1 for negative. So 8 bits run from minus 128 up to plus 127. Which pattern in the negative group means minus one?

groups.label: Negative (MSB 1)
groups.ask: What is the range of an 8-bit signed number?

explain.say: Last box: group the bits in fours. 1111 is F and 1011 is B, so minus five is FB in hex. As a check, FB read as unsigned is 251, and 251 minus 256 is minus five. Well done! Challenge: what is minus twelve in 8-bit hex? Hint: twelve is 0000 1100.

faq.a: It is the way almost every processor stores signed whole numbers. To negate a number you flip all its bits and add one, so the same adder circuit handles both adding and subtracting.
asks: How do computers store negative numbers?

faq.q: Why do you flip the bits and add one?
faq.a: Flipping gives a pattern that adds to the original to make all ones, which is 2 to the n minus 1. Adding one makes the pair sum to exactly 2 to the n, which overflows to zero in n bits, so the pattern behaves as minus the number.
asks: Why add one after inverting the bits?

faq.q: How do I convert binary to hex?
faq.a: Split the binary number into groups of four bits from the right, then write each group as one hex digit from 0 to F. For example 1111 1011 is F and B, so FB.
asks: How do you change binary into hexadecimal?

faq.q: What is the range of an 8-bit signed number?
faq.a: With two's complement, 8 bits hold minus 128 up to plus 127. In general n bits hold minus 2 to the power n minus 1, up to 2 to the power n minus 1, minus one.
asks: Why is there one more negative number than positive?

faq.a: Overflow happens when a result is too big for the bits available, so it wraps round. In 8 bits, 127 plus 1 gives 1000 0000, which reads as minus 128. Programmers avoid it by using a wider type or checking results.
asks: What happens when a number is too big for its bits?

facts: An 8-bit two's complement number ranges from −128 to +127.
In December 2014 YouTube moved its view counter to 64-bit integers after Gangnam Style neared 2,147,483,647 views, the 32-bit signed limit.
One hex digit stands for exactly four bits, so a byte is always two hex digits.

quiz.say: What is minus twelve in 8-bit two's complement?
quiz.why: Twelve is 0000 1100. Flip it to 1111 0011, add one to get 1111 0100, which is F4 in hex.

wrong.1: That is sign and magnitude: a sign bit stuck on 12. Processors do not store integers that way.
wrong.2: That is only the flip, the one's complement. You still need to add one.

quiz.say: What does 0111 1111 plus 1 give in an 8-bit signed register?
quiz.show: What does 0111 1111 + 1 give in an 8-bit signed register?
quiz.why: The sum is 1000 0000. Its top bit is 1, so in two's complement it reads as minus 128: the number has overflowed.

wrong.1: Plus 128 needs 9 bits as a signed number, so it cannot fit; the pattern wraps round.
wrong.2: Zero comes from 1111 1111 plus 1, not from 0111 1111 plus 1.
